name: Boeing 747
headline: length
subtitle: 747-8, the longest version
description: The Boeing 747 'jumbo jet' first flew in 1969 and is known for its hump-shaped upper deck. Its final version, the 747-8, is also the longest: Boeing's airport planning document gives it a length of 250 ft 2 in (76.25 m), a wingspan of 224 ft 5 in (68.40 m) and a maximum takeoff weight of 987,000 lb.

measures.label: Length
measures.note: 747-8 overall length (250 ft 2 in); earlier 747 versions were shorter

measures.label: Tail height
measures.note: Ground to top of the tail, varying with loading and attitude (62 ft 3 in to 64 ft 0 in)

sources.title: 747-8 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58326-3, Rev D, December 2024)

caveats: Figures are for the 747-8. Earlier versions such as the 747-400 were shorter; their planning document could not be retrieved, so no figure for them is shown.
